ai.description: *Micrixalus spelunca* is a small frog (20–25 mm) with a brown dorsum and pale yellow throat. It is identified by its white-tipped toes and the male’s characteristic foot-flagging behavior.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micrixalus spelunca* is best distinguished by its unique, pale-colored, translucent-looking skin and significantly reduced eye size, adaptations to its cave-dwelling habitat.
ai.habitat: *Micrixalus spelunca* inhabits moist, evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically residing near rocky, shaded streams at elevations between 400 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Cave Dancing Frog is primarily nocturnal, exhibiting unique foot-flagging displays to communicate with rivals and potential mates near fast-flowing forest streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micrixalus spelunca* breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of unpigmented eggs in subterranean stream beds, where larvae develop within the gravel.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micrixalus spelunca* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, specifically found in the states of Karnataka and Kerala at elevations between 400 and 1,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Cave Dancing Frog produces a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short, metallic chirps while perched near rocky, fast-flowing streams in dark, cavernous habitats.
